title: Instacart: Detection Engineer II
description:
Headquarters:  Canada - Remote (ON, AB, BC, or NS Only)
 

   We're transforming the grocery industry  
  At Instacart, we invite the world to share love through food because we believe everyone should have access to the food they love and more time to enjoy it together. Where others see a simple need for grocery delivery, we see exciting complexity and endless opportunity to serve the varied needs of our community. We work to deliver an essential service that customers rely on to get their groceries and household goods, while also offering safe and flexible earnings opportunities to Instacart Personal Shoppers.  
 Instacart has become a lifeline for millions of people, and we’re building the team to help push our shopping cart forward. If you’re ready to do the best work of your life, come join our table. 
  Instacart is a Flex First team   
 There’s no one-size fits all approach to how we do our best work. Our employees have the flexibility to choose where they do their best work—whether it’s from home, an office, or your favorite coffee shop—while staying connected and building community through regular in-person events.  Learn more about our flexible approach to where we work.     Overview  
 Instacart's Detection Engineering team sits at the core of our Security organization, building and operating the systems that identify, surface, and respond to threats across one of North America's largest grocery technology platforms. We own the full detection lifecycle, from telemetry collection and signal design to automated response, across a complex, cloud-native environment spanning endpoint, cloud, container, and SaaS. 
 As a Detection Engineer, you'll be a technical anchor on the team: developing high-fidelity detection logic, hunting for novel attacker techniques, and raising the bar for how we think about coverage, quality, and scale. You'll work closely with Engineering, Red Team, Incident Response, Fraud, and Trust & Safety to ensure our detections reflect real-world adversary behavior (and not just signatures). 
 We operate with a detection-as-code mindset: everything we build is versioned, tested, and deployed through repeatable pipelines. We care deeply about reducing noise, improving analyst efficiency through automation and SOAR, and continuously evolving our coverage as the threat landscape shifts. 
 If you're energized by hard forensic problems, enjoy translating attacker TTPs into durable detection logic, and want to help shape the future of a growing security function, this role is for you. 
  About the Job  
 
 Develop, tune, document, and maintain detection logic across multiple log sources including endpoint, cloud, container, and SaaS products. 
 Assist in cyber forensic investigations across a variety of log sources 
 Optimize log ingestion pipelines and telemetry collection to ensure high-quality, actionable security data while managing volume and cost 
 Design and build SOAR playbooks and automation workflows to streamline detection triage, enrichment, and response actions 
 Mentor/knowledge share with other detection engineers on threat hunting methodologies, detection logic development, and investigation techniques 
 
  About You  
 Minimum Qualifications 
 
 2+ years of experience in a detection engineering, incident response, or offensive security role. 
 Experience with 1 or more public cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, GCP) 
 Deep understanding of attacker TTPs across modern zero trust environments, including identity compromise, token theft, and abuse of trust boundaries 
 Proficient understanding of macOS internals and telemetry available to identify macOS specific threats 
 Experience implementing detection-as-code workflows including version control, peer review processes, automated testing, and CI/CD deployment pipelines 
 Basic proficiency with Python, Golang, or other programming/scripting languages 
 Relevant certifications: GCFA, GCFE, GNFA, GREM, OSCP, GCIA, or similar 
 
 Preferred Qualifications 
 
 Background in offensive security or red teaming 
 Knowledge of machine learning for threat detection

 Through the channel, a great product only wins when the partner knows how to sell it. At Abnormal, we want every partner ready to lead with the whole platform. 
 Abnormal is a channel-first company: nearly all of our transactions run through partners, which makes partner readiness a direct driver of revenue. As Channel Enablement Manager, you will own how our reseller, distributor, and referral partners learn to position, sell, and support the full Abnormal platform, and how our internal sellers work alongside them. We are expanding from email security into a multi-product behavioral platform spanning Identity, Insider Risk, and AI Security, so partners need to lead with the platform and grow every customer over time. You will be the person who makes that possible. 
 This is a high-visibility individual contributor role on the Sales Enablement team, working closely with Channel Leadership, Channel Account Managers (CAMs), and Channel SEs. You will build scalable, role-based partner enablement and certifications, deliver training people remember, and use data to prove that enabled partners generate more pipeline and win more deals. It is a role for someone who loves the craft of helping others succeed and wants to bring AI to the center of how enablement scales. 
 What You Will Do 
 
  Build the framework.  Design, build, and deliver a role-based partner enablement framework (Partner Essentials, Partner Sales 101, Pre-Sales 101, and advanced modules) through the Partner Portal and live sessions. 
  Get partners productive faster.  Lead partner onboarding that takes new and focus partners from signed to productive, with clear readiness milestones and certification paths. 
  Train with impact.  Deliver engaging in-person and virtual training to partner sellers, SEs, and leaders on Abnormal's value proposition, SEG displacement, discovery, qualification, and competitive positioning. 
  Teach partners to sell the platform.  Enable partners to sell Abnormal as a platform, with clear land-and-expand plays, cross-sell motions, and readiness for every new product launch. 
  Prepare our own teams to co-sell.  Enable Abnormal AEs, SDRs, and SEs on how to work with partners, including rules of engagement, deal registration, channel discounts, and renewal incumbency. 
  Create the assets partners use.  Partner with CAMs, Channel SEs, Channel Ops, Channel Marketing, and Product Marketing to deliver partner-facing sales plays, use cases, win wires, campaigns-in-a-box, and competitive intelligence. 
  Let the data steer.  Use performance data (partner-sourced pipeline, deal reg conversion, certification completion, win rates) to find gaps, prioritize investments, and report measurable impact. 
  Scale with AI.  Use AI to scale enablement and reduce CAM 1:1 training time, through AI-assisted content, roleplays, and on-demand coaching, so CAMs can focus on pipeline generation and partner-sourced revenue.

You will also shape the region's go-to-market strategy, expansion plans, and capacity model. In this role, you will act as the COO to the VP of AMER Enterprise Sales, ensuring our business is growing efficiently and effectively.  Shape GTM strategy and org structure for AMER Enterprise by region and sales motion, setting the team up to win as enterprise AI demand grows. 
 
 
 Build the analysis behind regional expansion decisions, such as which territories to enter next and in what sequence, so we invest where the opportunity is largest. 
 
 
 Design region- and motion-specific SPIFFs, then measure whether they changed behavior and results. 
 
 
  Annual planning and capacity (in partnership with Strategy and Planning)  
 
 
 Support quota setting for the region, bringing field context to top-down targets so quotas are both ambitious and attainable.

About Us   AI coding is the largest use case of enterprise AI adoption today, as is evident from the success of Anthropic on Claude Code, Cursor’s $60B exit to SpaceX, and Cognition’s $48B valuation. Vulnerabilities are piling up 16x faster than companies can fix them, and adversaries are able to exploit these new vulnerabilities within hours.  AURI by  Endor Labs  closes that gap. Job Mission   Terraformation ’s mission is to accelerate global forest restoration by enabling high-quality, biodiverse restoration projects that deliver meaningful climate, community, and ecological outcomes. The Carbon Business Unit is a critical engine for that mission, creating the capital and commercial pathways that allow restoration projects to develop and scale.  Reporting to the VP, Carbon Development & Markets, the Global Head of Commercialization leads the CBU’s revenue and market function. They are responsible for transforming  Terraformation ’s project portfolio into credible, well-structured commercial opportunities for carbon buyers and capital providers. This leader will build an integrated approach to revenue strategy, buyer engagement, pricing, project finance, and deal execution, ensuring commercial commitments remain aligned with technical readiness, implementation reality, legal risk, and long-term project economics. The role will also help build a repeatable commercialization system that can scale as  Terraformation  expands its global portfolio.  
  Location:  Remote (Americas or Europe Preferred) 
  Salary:  $120,000 - $150,000 plus equity (depending on location and experience) 
  Responsibilities   
  Own the CBU commercialization strategy across carbon credit sales, offtake and ERPA structures, project finance, investor engagement, pricing, and market positioning, translating portfolio priorities into a clear commercial plan.  
  Build and manage a disciplined commercial pipeline and operating cadence, establishing clear conversion priorities, account ownership, forecasts, pricing assumptions, next steps, and escalation points across buyers and capital providers.  
  Lead commercial strategy and execution for priority transactions, including developing recommendations on pricing, structuring, negotiation strategy, counterparty positioning, and coordinating offtakes, ERPAs, prepayments, blended finance solutions, and other strategic transactions within approved commercial parameters as provided by the VP, Carbon Development & Markets.   
  Ensure commercial commitments remain grounded in project readiness and delivery confidence by partnering closely with Project Design & Development, Project Implementation, Legal, and Finance on timing, carbon volumes, economics, risk allocation, and contractual obligations, and ensure forward sales and ERPAs follow established stage-gate requirements or documented exception processes.  
  Develop and maintain senior relationships with buyers, investors, and strategic partners, positioning  Terraformation  as a credible, sophisticated, and high-integrity counterpart in the global carbon market.  
  Ensure strong post-signing commercial and client management, coordinating delivery obligations, milestones, buyer communications, contractual requirements, and emerging commercial risks across the CBU.  
  Build and lead a high-performing Commercialization team, setting clear priorities and accountability across Project Finance & Structuring, Sales / Client Success, and analytical support while coaching and developing team members to exercise strong commercial judgment and increasing ownership.  
  Build repeatable commercialization systems, tools, and standards—including pricing frameworks, pipeline discipline, transaction processes, and decision tools—that improve commercial execution and can scale across projects and geographies.  
  Provide clear commercial insight and recommendations to CBU leadership, informing portfolio prioritization, project stage-gate decisions, capital allocation, and trade-offs between market opportunity, project economics, and delivery capacity.  
   Minimum Qualifications   
  10+ years of relevant commercial experience, including significant leadership experience in the voluntary carbon market and a demonstrated track record of transacting carbon credits at meaningful scale.

 In 1967, John Shepherd-Barron reached his bank minutes after closing and could not get at his own money. In the bath that evening, he thought of a chocolate bar dispenser and swapped the chocolate for cash. On 27 June, outside a Barclays branch on Enfield High Street, an actor named Reg Varney drew £10 from the world's first cash machine. It took a four-digit code (originally six, until his wife told him nobody remembers six). The bank's hours had stopped being the customer's problem. 
 Nearly sixty years later, the bar has moved, but the test hasn't: a personal financial product is judged on whether it fits the life of the person using it. Mercury is building personal banking* to that standard. 
 Personal Banking is how Mercury earns a place in someone's financial life. We're looking for a Head of Product to own it end-to-end: setting product strategy, leading a team of product managers, driving growth and engagement, and owning business performance.
